html:
The land of the Batammariba people in northeastern Togo, stretching into Benin, known for its takienta, fortress-like houses of mud with round towers and granaries.

Each house is built as a small world, a sign of the family and its ancestors, with shrines at the door and grain stored on the roof. The Batammariba resisted outside rule for long and kept their customs of initiation and building. UNESCO listed Koutammakou as a World Heritage Site in 2004 as a living cultural landscape. On the Benin side the same houses are called tata somba. See also German Togoland and UNESCO.
